CweFindings.Name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
CweFindings.Description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.
CweFindings.Explanation: Anonymous GET / calls getAllPhotos and a native query selecting every row including photo_data into List<Photo>. The byte[] LOB has default eager fetching and the query has neither pagination nor total-byte limit. Uploaded BLOB count and aggregate size are not bounded; an uploader can grow stored content and any public gallery request materializes that aggregate in the JVM heap (container default maximum 512 MB), permitting excessive allocation and denial of service. Per-file 10 MB and per-request 50 MB upload limits do not bound accumulated gallery allocation.

CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: Security-critical photo upload and deletion logs record file/record identifiers and outcomes but omit authenticated principal and request source/correlation information. DetailController.deletePhoto and PhotoServiceImpl.uploadPhoto have no principal/request audit context; SecurityConfig configures HTTP Basic without an application audit handler or authentication-event log listener. Existing mutation logs cannot identify the requesting actor/source for investigation. This is insufficient audit context, not a claim that all application logging is absent; infrastructure access/audit logging was not supplied.

CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoServiceImpl.uploadPhoto trusts caller-supplied Content-Type. If ImageIO finds no reader, the code still stores original arbitrary bytes as a photo; a non-IOException decoder failure is also ignored. An authenticated uploader can submit non-image or polyglot content labeled image/png and it is persisted and publicly returned by servePhoto. No content/declared-type consistency check is enforced. This confirms upload-type validation bypass, not server-side script execution; browser execution is not established (Spring Security supplies nosniff).

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: createPhotoCard interpolates originalFileName from upload JSON without HTML or attribute escaping into img alt, title and element content, and displayNewPhotos passes the resulting markup to insertAdjacentHTML. showErrors likewise interpolates user-controlled local or returned filenames into innerHTML. A crafted filename containing markup or an attribute breakout is interpreted as DOM content in the uploading browser. Normal server-rendered Thymeleaf views use escaped th:text; persistent execution on another viewer is not established.
